newsitem.title: LEBANON: Talks on new government near conclusion - sources.
newsitem.headline: Talks on new government near conclusion - sources.

text.p: Lebanon's leaders met on Thursday evening amid indications they had resolved disputes over the distribution of cabinet posts and would soon announce formation of a new government.
"Major problems have been solved and the new cabinet will in principle be announced later in the evening if nothing new comes up," an official source told Reuters.
The source spoke as Prime Minister-designate Rafik al-Hariri met President Elias Hrawi for the second time in the day. The two were joined by parliament Speaker Nabih Berri.
"The new cabinet will comprise 30 ministers, including Hariri, just like the outgoing cabinet, and key ministers are coming back," another source said.
Syria, Lebanon's main power broker with 35,000 troops there, has been trying to end disputes between the three leaders over the composition of the new cabinet.
Hariri, nominated on October 24 to form his third government following parliamentary elections, was expected to complete it last week but ran into difficulties, first with Hrawi and then with Berri.
According to official sources the disputes centred on distribution of key portfolios between the religious communities the three leaders represent -- Christian, Sunni Moslem and Shiite Moslem.
Hariri told reporters earlier on Thursday after a meeting with Hrawi he expected the government to be formed soon.
